text:
Julia: Heads up — saw a regression in streaming throughput and a couple OOM spikes during the long-chat perf run this morning. Attaching quick profiler dump and mem trace excerpts.

Mike: Can you drop the small trace here? which branch/sha?

Julia: main@a7c3f9 (canary from yesterday). Repro command I used: `python tools/repro_long_chat.py --model redwood-7b --seq 8192 --batch 4 --trace mem,allocs`

Julia: profiler snippet (nvprof-like):
```
GPU kernel time breakdown:
 - attention_kernel_fp16: 42.3%
 - attention_kernel_int8_fallback: 18.9%
 - kv_read_kernel: 9.2%
 - kv_compact_copy: 6.4%
 - allocator_free: 3.1%
Peak memory: 15.1 GB / 24 GB
Frequent OOM signal emitted at step ~1200 (large prefix).
```

Dennis: Interesting — I think kernel routing picked an fp16->int8 fallback path mid-run because of sequence-length-driven kernel selection. That fallback allocates extra staging buffers which interact poorly with the chunk allocator.

Sara: We rolled batching heuristic tweak in canary two days ago (PR #4127) that increases max coalesce window. Might be increasing transient alloc counts. Not sure if it's correlated.

infra-bot: deploy canary/main@a7c3f9 started for eng-runtime-ci (job 2391).

Mike: I pulled the memtrace. Most of the churn is tiny (<= 64KB) GPU allocations for KV tiles, and a few large contiguous allocations for attention workspace. The chunk allocator ends up with lots of holes between active blocks.

Mike: pprof-like heap top:
```
0.35 GB  23%  23%  kv_tile_alloc (64KB x ~4300)
1.92 GB  40%  63%  attention_workspace (several grows to 512MB)
0.12 GB  44%  67%  temporary_staging (spill buffers)
```

Julia: The compaction/eviction only runs on idle and it's not triggering because the worker loop never hits the idle path during long prefixes. So fragmentation accumulates.

Dennis: Two ideas: 1) force opportunistic compaction on allocation path when fragmentation crosses threshold (cheap check + background copy), 2) pre-reserve bigger contiguous workspace for attention to avoid mid-run grow. Both have trade-offs (copy cost vs peak reservation).

Sara: compaction cost is the pain point — kv_compact_copy is a GPU memcpy kernel and at our sizes it's non-trivial (~20-30ms on 40MB moves). That can spike tail latency if done inline. We could make it async and throttle.

Julia: Proposal: (A) enable a per-stream soft-reserve factor for attention workspace (1.2x) to cut grow events, (B) add a fast-path in allocator: try coalesce adjacent free chunks within the same slab without full compaction, (C) on OOM try a spill-to-host fallback for oversized KV entries and mark those chunks reusable ASAP.

Mike: +1 to A/B. For C we should be careful — spilling changes perf characteristics for users. Add guard by env var and only enable in dev/dedicated-experiment.

Dennis: I'll prototype a coalesce-only routine that does address-table stitching (no copy) for adjacent free segments within a bucket. If coalesce fails due to fragmentation we fallback to scheduling an async compaction job to run on separate stream.

Sara: Test plan — run the long-chat reproducer with: `python tools/repro_long_chat.py --model redwood-7b --seq 8192 --batch 8 --trace mem,kv --alloc-tweak reserve=1.2 coalesce=1` and collect p50/p95/p99 tokens/sec and p99 latency.

infra-bot: Job queued: perf-long-chat-1998523 (job 2399) — you'll get updates when complete.

Julia: I'll open a small PR with the reserve tweak + env guard and add metrics for "compaction-time" and "coalesce-hit-rate". Will also include a simple benchmark harness.

Mike: sgtm. Please add a feature-flag so we can A/B rollout to canary only. Also log every forced-compact reason (threshold, allocation-fail, idle).

Sara: I'll run an A/B pair after the PR lands and paste the diff of memory profiles here. If coalesce reduces kv_compact_copy by >50% we can consider enabling coalesce in dedicated.

Dennis: Note: watch for kernel selection regressions — if pre-reserving increases average seq footprint it might push more runs into the int8 fallback. We'll tune the routing thresholds accordingly.

Julia: Thanks all. Action items: Dennis prototype coalesce (EOD), Julia PR for reserve/metrics (WIP), Sara run A/B perf tests when PR merged, Mike add logging/flag gating.

Mike: :thumbsup:

Sara: :rocket:

Julia: I'll follow up with the profiler flamegraphs when the infra job completes.
